title: Post-Deployment Safety Checklist & Runbook Updates after Canary Rollout Abort
creator: Liam Carter
description:
Summary: During yesterday's canary rollout of v2.3.0 for the text-generation endpoint, the automated canary evaluation marked increased hallucination rate and latency regressions at 12% traffic. The rollout executed an auto-abort, but investigation revealed gaps in the safety checks, insufficient shadow-traffic isolation, and unclear rollback telemetry. This ticket captures runbook updates, concrete safety checklist items, and follow-ups to prevent recurrence.

Goals:
- Consolidate incident learnings into the model lifecycle runbook.
- Add deterministic safety checks and metric thresholds to the canary evaluator.
- Harden shadow-traffic flows and ensure non-production effects are isolated.
- Implement additional automated abort/rollback criteria and post-rollback validation.

Scope (what this ticket will deliver):
- Updated runbook doc with step-by-step abort, verify, and fascia steps.
- New canary check definitions (latency P95, hallucination score delta, generation token error rate) and guardrails.
- A/B test template updates to include preflight validation and minimum sample size gating.
- Scripts and dashboards to validate that rollback did not leak model outputs into production logs.

Out of scope: full redesign of canary system (addressed separately in ENG-7180).
acceptance_criteria: Runbook updated in Confluence and linked in the deployment pipeline
Canary evaluator includes at least three deterministic checks with clear thresholds
Shadow traffic is configured to never write to production indices/logs; validation shows zero writes for a 1-hour test
Automated rollback sequence performs post-rollback health checks and notifies stakeholders
Playbook reviewed and approved by SRE and PM (commented and signed off)

comments: 2026-03-02 Liam Carter: Initial triage — Canary aborted at 12% due to hallucination_score delta +0.12 and P95 latency +60ms. No customer-facing errors reported, but quality regressions exceeded threshold.

2026-03-03 Asha Patel: Triage meeting notes attached. Key takeaway: our canary evaluator relies too heavily on sampling that undercounts edge-case prompt behaviors. Need deterministic prompt set and larger sample size for early traffic percentages.
2026-03-04 Marco Reed: Proposed metric 'hallucination_delta' implemented in staging evaluator; threshold candidate 0.07. Will validate against historical runs this week.
2026-03-06 Priya Nambiar: Found that one shadow consumer was still writing debug tokens to 'prod-logs' during the rollout due to env var misconfiguration. Fix is staged; audit will be run post-fix.

2026-03-08 SRE Team: Agreed to add post-rollback smoke tests and a verification window before reattempting rollout. Also recommended adding an observable flag when auto-rollback triggers to assist on-call.
2026-03-09 PM Review (Dana Liu): Suggested including stakeholder notification templates and a standard Slack channel naming scheme for future rollouts. Adding to runbook.
2026-03-10 Liam Carter: Consolidated checklist and assigned owners. Moving to 'In Progress' while engineering completes tasks.
postmortem_summary: Auto-abort of v2.3.0 canary prevented the release from reaching customers. Root causes: (1) insufficient canary metric set that missed a quality regression signal until 12% traffic, (2) a misconfigured shadow consumer that wrote debug data to prod indices, and (3) lack of post-rollback verification. Remediations include runbook updates, deterministic canary checks, shadow isolation audits, and new post-rollback smoke tests.
